title: A characterization for tightness of the sparse Moment-SOS hierarchy
authors: Nie, Jiawang and Qu, Zheng and Tang, Xindong and Zhang, Linghao
relevance: Closest finite exactness boundary: Theorem 3.1 (pp. 377–378) characterizes finite sparse SOS exactness through local truncated quadratic-module certificates with polynomial separator messages. Example 6.7 (p. 393) gives a two-bag [-1,1]^3 instance with optimum 1 whose required separator is -1/(1+x2^2), so the sparse hierarchy is not tight at any finite order although the dense order-2 SOS certificate is exact. This is a qualitative obstruction, not a rate.

title: Finite convergence and minimizer extraction in moment relaxations with correlative sparsity
relevance: Most direct finite local-to-global result: Theorem 1.1 (p. 2) constructs a global atomic K-representing measure for finite sparse moments under RIP, local moment and localizing PSD, clique flatness rank M^ω_Δi = rank M^(ω−di)_Δi, and predecessor-separator flatness rank M^ω_(Δi∩Δj) = rank M^(ω−1)_(Δi∩Δj). Corollary 1.2 gives finite hierarchy exactness. Flatness is essential to this theorem; it does not extend arbitrary feasible pseudo-moments. Theorem 1.3 (p. 3) separately states the infinite-sequence/local Archimedean measure result attributed to Lasserre.

title: Convergence rates for sums-of-squares hierarchies with correlative sparsity
authors: Korda, Milan and Magron, Victor and Ríos-Zertuche, Rodolfo
relevance: Strongest prior quantitative sparse comparison. Theorem 6 (p. 444) gives a sparse box full-preordering degree/rate O(R^(−2/(w+3))) under RIP. Theorem 8 (pp. 445–446) treats sparse ordinary quadratic modules on compact semialgebraic domains under RIP, normalized local generators, local Archimedean certificates, and local Łojasiewicz error bounds; for local exponent 1 its displayed degree conditions yield the fixed-data rate O(R^(−18/(238+55w))). It proves sparse positivity and hierarchy convergence under those stronger hypotheses, but gives no finite global measure extension for every feasible local pseudo-moment collection.

title: Squared polynomial approximation kernels for the hypercube: improved error bounds and implications for Lasserre hierarchies
authors: Gribling, Sander and de Klerk, Etienne and Vera, Juan C.
relevance: Dense ordinary-module baseline and kernel antecedent: Theorem 7 (p. 13) proves an O(log^3(r)/r^2) lower-bound gap for the dense quadratic module on [-1,1]^n under n|r and r/log_2(r) ≥ c2 n^2 d^2, with explicit constants. It supplies no overlapping-bag separator consistency or sparse gluing theorem.

title: On the convergence rates of moment-SOS hierarchies approximation of truncated moment sequences
authors: Tran, Hoang Anh and Toh, Kim-Chuan
relevance: Published dense finite-moment comparator. Theorem 3.5 (arXiv v1 pp. 15–16) bounds the Hausdorff distance from fixed-degree pseudo-moments to actual moments on products of balls/simplexes at O(r^−2), but the hierarchy is the full preordering and the theorem assumes a redundant ball inequality. Theorems 4.7 and Corollary 4.8 treat compact semialgebraic sets under an error-bound exponent. It does not address overlapping sparse bags or separator gluing.

title: On the convergence rates of moment-SOS hierarchies approximation of truncated moment sequences
authors: Tran, Hoang Anh and Toh, Kim-Chuan
relevance: Preprint version of the work published online in Mathematical Programming on 7 July 2026 (listed separately in this lane). Theorem 3.5 (pp. 15–16) establishes O(r^−2) fixed-degree pseudo-moment approximation to actual moments for products of unit balls and standard simplexes with a redundant ball constraint, using the full preordering. It is dense and does not give sparse overlap gluing.

title: The Effective Countable Generalized Moment Problem
relevance: Closest abstract framework for moment consistency across several measures. Theorem 2.11 (p. 12) gives a fixed-degree Hausdorff approximation rate for truncated GMP feasibility sets with countably many moment constraints under S-fullness (Assumption 1.3), attained infinite-dimensional dual optimizer (Assumption 1.9), and Archimedean local modules (Assumption 2.1). It can model separator moment equalities conditionally, but the attained-dual assumption is exactly the polynomial-separator obstruction absent from the manuscript's finite construction.

title: Extension on the convergence rates of moment-SOS hierarchies via approximation of truncated moment sequences
authors: Tran, Hoang Anh and Toh, Kim-Chuan
relevance: New dense Putinar extension posted six days before the cutoff. Theorem 3.7 (pp. 16–17) bounds fixed-k Hausdorff distance of pseudo-moments from true moments for nonempty X⊆[0,1]^n with box constraints xi(1−xi)≥0, normalized ||gj||_(1,mon)≤1, equalities hi=0, and a global Łojasiewicz error bound d(x,X)≤cL p(x)^L. For fixed data the induced rate is O(log^(3L/2)(r)/r^L). It strengthens dense Putinar approximation but does not impose or exploit sparse overlap consistency.
